narrative:
The model estimates there’s a 32% chance you won’t pass your final year, which is above the 10% threshold that requires extra support. Because of this, you’ll need to take remedial courses to help you stay on track.

The main reasons the model is concerned come down to three key areas. First, your father’s education level stands out—most students who don’t need remedial courses have fathers with at least some secondary education or higher, while yours completed only primary school. This factor slightly increases the risk of struggling in your final year.

On a more positive note, you’ve never failed a class before, which is a strong point in your favor. Most students in your situation also have a clean record, and this significantly lowers the predicted risk. The reason you chose this school—because it’s close to home—also works in your favor, as students who pick schools for other reasons, like reputation or specific courses, tend to perform slightly better.

To improve your chances, focus on increasing your study time, as you currently spend less than two hours a week, while most students who pass dedicate at least two to five hours. The remedial courses will give you structured support, but you can also take steps at home, like setting aside more time for review and seeking help from family or teachers when needed. Small changes now can make a big difference by the end of the year.
